title: Discrepancy between self-report and neurophysiological markers of socio-affective responses in lonely individuals
description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG recordings and behavioral ratings from 148 healthy adults performing an Emotion Processing and Regulation task using static emotional images. The study examines discrepancies between self-reported and neurophysiological socio-affective responses in relation to loneliness, using a factorial design manipulating stimulus content (social/non-social) and regulation instructions (watch-neutral, watch-negative, reappraise-negative). Participants rated arousal and valence after viewing each stimulus, enabling analysis of the relationship between subjective and physiological emotional responses.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a 64-channel QuickCap and Neuroscan SynampsRT amplifier at 1000 Hz sampling rate, with impedances kept below 5 kΩ. Additional sensors included horizontal and vertical EOG, EKG, and GSR/EDA. Preprocessing was performed in MATLAB using EEGLAB and ERPLAB, including band-pass filtering (0.1–30 Hz), downsampling to 250 Hz, average mastoid re-referencing, automatic bad-channel rejection (clean_rawdata), ICA with ADJUST/SASICA component rejection, spherical interpolation, epoching (-200 to 5000 ms), baseline correction, artifact rejection, and condition averaging.
